newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Strikers at Namibian copper mine take manager hostage.
newsitem.headline: Strikers at Namibian copper mine take manager hostage.

text.p: Striking copper miners at Tsumeb Corp Ltd in Namibia have taken the mine manager hostage in the increasingly bitter labour dispute now entering its sixth week, owners Gold Fields Namibia Ltd said on Tuesday.

A company spokesman told Reuters from Namibia that strikers from the Mineworkers' Union of Namibia (MUN) had forced their way onto mine manager Tony De Beers' property on Monday, but been ejected by police.
However, on Tuesday they returned to gather outside the property -- effectively trapping De Beers and his wife inside.
"They are all round his house and have blocked access to the property. There is no way he is going to try and drive through that," the spokesman said.
Mediation efforts to halt the strike down last Thursday and violent protest flared over the weekend injuring eight people in clashes between strikers and police.
The company plans to put a settlement proposal by Friday and, if the union accepted it, negotiations could resume within the context of mediation or directly with management.
"The union can then come back to us directly or ask to go to mediation again," the spokesman said.
Striking miners occupied a hospital on Monday which the spokesman said had now been shut down. "The hospital was taken over and we have actually closed it now," he said.
The spokesman said that strikers were now in control of all three copper mines at the site -- Tsumeb, Kombat and Otjihase. "They are in total control," he said.
He said police were trying to regain control of the mines, but having little success.

The strike over pay began with TCL offering a seven percent rise and the union wanting 14.5 percent. The spokesman warned damage caused by the strike meant any new offer was unlikely to be as high as seven percent unless job losses were included in the package.
"We are back to where we started when the strike began."
Tsumeb mines and smelters have been shut down since August 23 when MUN members began to strike.
